posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text:
The afternoon holds 154 feeder visits, above the recent daily average of 115.6. Tufted Titmice account for 73 of those visits, and Carolina Chickadees for 34. A probable House Sparrow, Eastern Phoebe, and a House Finch joined the morning’s single Northern Cardinal at the feeder.

The Ruby-throated Hummingbird leads detections with 129, followed by Northern Cardinals at 123 and Blue Jays at 86. A Red-shouldered Hawk was detected eight times during the 13:00 hour.

The weather is calm with a high of 28.222 C and negligible wind. The last visual record occurred at 15:10, a House Finch.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text: Yesterday marked the busiest day in the past week, with 268 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, well above the seven-day average of 97 visits and 12 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees were the dominant visual presences, maintaining their status as regulars present every day this week. The station’s new seed feeder and treat bowl, installed over the past week, coincided with a significant increase in visitor diversity and frequency. A Black-capped Chickadee provided the station’s first confident visual record, joining a list that included a Common Gallinule, also a first visual for this location. The day closed with a final auditory detection of a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at 20:30. The high volume of detections, particularly from Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals, reflects the continued presence of the new microphone installed on September 13.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
September 14 was the station's busiest day this week, recording 16 species and 232 feeder visits, a significant jump from the prior seven-day average. Regulars like Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees held steady on the tube feeders, while Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays maintained their consistent presence throughout the week.

This surge in activity follows the station's recent hardware updates. A new seed feeder installed on September 13 resolved detection issues, and the switch to a new microphone source on the same day ensured clear audio data. These changes align with the increased visit counts and reliable detections observed today.

The day ended with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at sunset, capping a session where visual logs captured 11 species. While American Goldfinches and Eastern Screech-Owls were seen earlier in the week, they were absent today. The final hours brought quiet calls from Northern Cardinals and Carolina Wrens as the light faded.
